_README: Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

blocks.name: dat_FF76
blocks.note: CONFIRMED by inspection, no xrefs anywhere in traced code (checked): the first 10 bytes decode as ASCII 'GCC(c)1984' -- General Computer Corporation's own copyright/signature string, same exact pattern (identical size: 138 bytes, same relative position right after a bare JMP entry point) found in the Dig Dug (7800) project's own tail region -- independently re-confirmed here by reading this ROM's own bytes, not assumed from that project. Followed by ~122 bytes with no discernible structure (not ASCII, no repeating pattern, no xrefs) -- almost certainly unused filler/padding. Ends with the hardware vectors at $FFFA-$FFFF (NMI=$B15D, RESET=$FF73, IRQ=$B610 -- byte-verified against the already-declared entries), which is why this was showing as a gap despite being fully accounted for: vector bytes are data, not executed code.

blocks.name: dat_DF50
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: every one of this ROM's 50 already-labeled dat_ sub-tables sitting inside this 8227-byte span (starting with dat_DF50 itself, real xref rom:B8CF) already carries a real cross-reference from already-traced code -- checked programmatically across the whole span, not spot-checked. Also swept for any JSR/JMP in the traced program landing anywhere in this range (the chr_rom_C000-style bug this project's sibling projects learned to check for): none found. Declared as one block to stop 8227 bytes of already-correctly-referenced data from showing as an unclaimed gap. This is the single largest untraced span in the ROM and has not been characterized further yet -- whether it's one resource or several hasn't been determined.
